summary: Open Interest Ep.21 (Apr 2026): Babbage explains Gresham Quant's commodity-only alternative-markets trend program: structural market selection, capacity discipline, trend quality (autocorrelation) and execution with a risk-budgeted desk that waits passively.

coverage.note: why commodities only, diversification and financialization
capacity discipline, factor diversity, capacity numbers
alternativeness metrics, speculators, trend quality vs quantity, curve position
inelastic supply, carbon examples, long/short symmetry
risk allocation, liquidity limits, broker network
clearing and swaps, execution costs and variance
discretionary-looking execution risk budget, passive fills
anti-correlated execution, vol-scaled positions, unfilled orders
liberation day, execution is systematic, client positioning

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: after 20 years of no trend that was probably the biggest commodity trend there was
claims.claim: Cocoa in 2024 delivered the biggest commodity trend after twenty years without one, but Gresham avoids it as too financialized, illustrating that trend can appear in markets without a prior trend record.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: One is just incrementally adding one market to your, you know, your 301st market really makes no difference to diversification.
claims.claim: Beyond a few hundred markets, adding another changes nothing because allocation to it is tiny and the effective degrees of freedom matter more than the count (2-, 5- and 10-year Treasuries are essentially one market).
claims.testable: yes - effective-N or marginal Sharpe tests

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: you're kind of side-stepping that whole collapse to one effect.
claims.claim: Financialized markets (FX, indices, fixed income) collapse to one in macro shocks, while less financialized commodities with structural differences stay resilient and diversifying.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: unless you have a real strong capacity discipline, your portfolio won't look diversified.
claims.claim: Alternative commodity diversification requires capacity discipline: with billions, allocation concentrates in crude, gold and gas so niche markets matter little. Gresham sees capacity around 1-2bn and soft-closed at about 1bn (half closed during COVID's high commodity volatility).
claims.conditions: Small AUM relative to market liquidity

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: the investment horizon that we think is is relevant for a trend strategy is not months or even a year, it's several years.
claims.claim: Trend investors need a horizon of several years, so leave headroom so existing clients can benefit from organic growth instead of closing after a 15-20% year.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: last year we dropped 44 markets and we added 31.
claims.claim: Gresham trades about 150 markets and turned over roughly a quarter of the list in 2025 (44 dropped, 31 added), selecting on market structure rather than backtests.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: So, the first thing I would say it's not based on the back test, right?
claims.claim: Choosing markets by backtest Sharpe is data mining and 'the key to future misery'; instead evaluate who trades the market, where on the curve, and its correlation to mainstream commodities.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: you know, if there's an expensive oil spread that looks alternative from a low liquidity perspective, that that's not interesting to us if it's going to be highly correlated to mainstream crude.
claims.claim: 'Alternativeness' means low correlation to mainstream commodities (for example the Bloomberg Commodity Index), not low liquidity or barriers to entry; a low-liquidity oil spread correlated with crude is just costly crude exposure.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: For us it's how many speculators are in this market? So, you can look at commit to the trader data.
claims.claim: Speculator participation (Commitments of Traders, share of open interest going to delivery vs recycled, broker queries, conference attendance) identifies alternative markets; when CTAs enter, the market is becoming financialized and less interesting.
claims.indicator: COT data; open interest to delivery

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: There's a drift component, which I'd call kind of like the quantity of trend, how far a market moves. And there's an auto correlation component, which I would label as the quality of the trend.
claims.claim: Trend splits into drift (quantity) and autocorrelation (quality); both are better in alternative commodities than mainstream ones over 30 years, linked to low speculative activity.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: the front of that curve is a financialized speculator dominated kind of noise news driven market.
claims.claim: Further along a commodity curve (about 5 years out) hedgers dominate, giving smoother, higher-autocorrelation trends than the noisy speculative front; trading deferred contracts improves trend quality.
claims.indicator: curve position of trend (front vs far)

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: there's an inelasticity in these sort of markets between supply and demand.
claims.claim: Inelastic supply (coal mines take decades to permit and keep running at a loss) and demand, plus shipping and storage frictions, mean imbalances clear only through large persistent price moves, a structural reason for trends in commodities.
claims.testable: partly - elasticity proxies could be used

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: we were looking at European carbon, which is at the time really the only carbon market around with any liquidity.
claims.claim: European carbon had negative trend Sharpe over its 8 years of history in 2016 but was added on structural criteria and became one of the best performers, an example of selecting on structure not backtest.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: Californian carbon scheme, there's an effective auction floor price each set each year.
claims.claim: In markets with a price floor (California carbon auction floor) the short trend is capped, so the model must be overridden to prevent adding to shorts near the floor.
claims.indicator: Californian carbon futures vs auction floor

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: we want to be able to get out of a max conviction long or short within, say, a week or so in a stress scenario.
claims.claim: Position limits are set so the largest position can be exited in about a week in stress; liquidity plus diversification determine top-line capacity, and new markets start with small weights until real fills confirm costs.
claims.direction: small initial weights in new markets

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: you cannot plug a computer into the exchange and just electronically trade. You have to do it through getting quotes
claims.claim: Niche commodity execution relies on a wide network of specialist brokers and dealers via phone quotes, which creates price competition and requires onboarding brokers when adding markets.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: Chinese commodity futures, we do via swap, but that that money is all kept offshore.
claims.claim: Chinese commodity futures are accessed through swaps with margin held by a third party to limit counterparty risk; all other markets are exchange-cleared futures.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: a typical liquid CTA, maybe they're spending, I don't know, say, 70 basis points a year. Maybe maybe even a percent on on slippage transaction costs.
claims.claim: Large CTAs lose roughly 0.7-1% a year to slippage, and splitting orders across the day benchmarks well against TWAP/VWAP but hides the autocorrelated cost.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: nearly all of that is just the positions you're holding. It's not the trades you're doing on a day
claims.claim: At 15% annual risk (about 1% daily variance), trades account for only about 5% of daily variance and are uncorrelated across markets, so execution risk is a small fraction of portfolio risk.
claims.indicator: share of daily variance from trading

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: we're going to give the desk a higher level of effective risk allocation, if you like.
claims.claim: Gresham gives the trading desk a risk budget (tracking error to model) and lets it work orders passively over several days with bounds, so the desk acts as an anti-correlated buffer and trend signals can be faster for the same cost.
claims.testable: yes - slippage with and without patience

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: normally fast signals are better before cost, right?
claims.claim: Faster signals look better before costs, but patient passive execution (avoiding crossing the spread, which in freight can be 100bp) preserves them after costs.
claims.direction: passive limit orders in wide-spread markets
claims.conditions: Largest benefit in wide-spread markets such as freight

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: Our slippage bill last year was effectively close to zero compared to previous years in in a relative sense.
claims.claim: Passive execution cut slippage close to zero over the first year, partly via invisible savings when the model changes its target before the order is done.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: You can kind of view it as the trading desk being an anti-correlated strategy to trend.
claims.claim: Passive waiting behaves as an anti-trend (mean-reverting) component, adding diversification so the strategy risk scale can be raised.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: So, yes, it went from 100 lots, nothing was done, and 120 lots, nothing was done.
claims.claim: If the market moves away, the unfilled trade accumulates tracking variance until the limit forces a trade, so slippage variance rises while the average cost falls; market near 50/50 each day gives savings about half the time.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: liberation day wasn't really an event.
claims.claim: In April 2025 big propane moves, the passive method of cutting positions saved slippage versus an aggressive exit that would have hit a move-away-and-back.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: You should go and find a cheap management fee only liquid trend that will go up when stock markets go down and won't cost you much, right?
claims.claim: Core trend with equity-shock convexity should come from cheap liquid trend; alternative-commodity trend is a diversifying addition with only 20-25% correlation to the SG CTA index.
claims.direction: add alternative commodity trend as a satellite

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: it shortcuts a lot of the kind of faith aspect you almost have to put into any any system or any signal
claims.claim: Signals with clear structural drivers (inelastic commodity supply) let investors keep faith through multi-year drawdowns, whereas opaque machine-learning signals get pulled after three years of weak results.

claims.speaker: Tom Babbage
claims.quote: there's a very strong and clear positive convexity for commodity trend and inflation and deflation.
claims.claim: Commodity trend protects a 60/40 portfolio in rising, high and low inflation periods, so adding even basic commodity trend improves results across inflation regimes (the 'Eras Tour' paper).
claims.indicator: commodity trend returns vs inflation regime
